original.reason: The key identity ν₂(x+a)=min(ν₂(x),ν₂(a)) is false when the valuations are equal: e.g. x=a=2 gives ν₂(x+a)=2, not 1. Thus Alice can increase the proposed potential. Also the odd-a argument overlooks N=1.

judgment.reason: Its even-a potential argument rests on the same false valuation identity, so it does not establish termination in that case.
The asserted valuation identity for even a is false when ν₂(x)=ν₂(a), invalidating the central potential argument.
The proof of the even-a case relies on the false equality ν₂(x+a)=min{ν₂(x),ν₂(a)}.
Its claimed non-increasing potential is unsupported because the valuation formula used to prove it is false, e.g. x=a=2.
